<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par100 />''circum, around''; others have quite ceased to be so used, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כְּבָר}} (length) ''long ago'' [Aram.: only in Ec.]; {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד}} (repetition, duration) ''again'' or ''further''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|d}}
(''c'') Adjectives, especially in the feminine (corresponding to the Indo-Germanic neuter), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רִֽאשׁוֹנָה|translate=primum, formerly}} (more frequently {{GHGheb|text=בָּרִֽאשׁוֹנָה}}, also {{GHGheb|text=לָרִאשׁוֹנָה}}); {{GHGheb|text=רַבָּה}} and {{GHGheb|text=רַבַּת}} [both rare] ''multum, much, enough''; {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָאוֹת|translate=wonderfully}} (properly ''mirabilibus'', sc. ''modis''), {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּדִית|translate=Jewish}}, i.e. in the Jewish language.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|e}}
(''d'') Verbs in the infinitive absolute, especially in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, which are likewise to be regarded as accusatives ({{GHGpar|113|h}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}} (prop. ''a multiplying'') ''much'' [frequent], {{GHGheb|text=לְהַרְבֵּה}} [rare and late] ''in multitude''; {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁכֵּם}} (''mane faciendo'') ''early''; {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֲרֵב}} (''vespere faciendo'') ''in the evening''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|f}}
(''e'') Pronouns and numerals, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} (prop. ''there=at this place'') ''here'', {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה|translate=here, hither}} (also of time, {{GHGheb|text=עַד־הֵ֫נָּה|translate=till now}}, cf. the late and rare {{GHGheb|text=עֲדֶן}} and {{GHGheb|text=עֲדֶ֫נָּה}}={{GHGheb|text=עַד־הֵן}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַחַת}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁתַּ֫יִם}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה|translate=once, twice, seven times, a hundred times}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁנִית|translate=for the second time}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|g}}
'''3.''' Some adverbs are formed by the addition of formative syllables (most frequently {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}}) to substantives or adjectives, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָמְנָם}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֻמְנָם|translate=truly}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אֹמֶן|translate=truth}}); {{GHGheb|text=חִנָּם}} (by favour) ''gratis'' (from {{GHGheb|text=חֵן|translate=gratia}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֵיקָם|translate=in vain}}, ''frustra'', but also ''empty'' (from {{GHGheb|text=רֵיק|translate=empty, emptiness, vanum}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=21}}, parallel with the {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=מְלֵאָה|translate=full}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹמָם|translate=by day}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}})<ref>Is this {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}} an instance of the locative or temporal termination (cf. especially {{GHGheb|text=צהרם}}) mentioned in {{GHGpar|88|c}}? Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xl. p. 721, considers {{GHGheb|text=יוֹמָם}} a secondary substantival form (used adverbially like {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יְלָה|translate=noctu}}), corresponding to the Phoenician and Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=ימם}}, Syr. ''ʾimāmā''; cf. on the other hand, König, ii. 255, who follows Olshausen in maintaining that the ''ām'' is an adverbial termination.</ref>; with ''ô'' in the last syllable, {{GHGheb|text=פִּתְאֹם}}, for {{GHGheb|text=פִּתְעֹם}}, ''in a twinkling, suddenly'' (from {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫תַע|translate=a twinkling}}, the ''ô'' being probably obscured from an original ''â'').<ref>{{GHGheb|text=דּוּמָם|translate=silent}} (an adjective in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=26}}; a substantive in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=19}}), which was formerly included under this head, is better taken, with Barth (''Nominalbildung'', p. 352, Rem. 2), as a participle formed like {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹבָב}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלָל}}, so that {{GHGheb|text=דּוּמָם}} (perhaps assimilated to {{GHGheb|text=דּוּמָה}}) stands for original {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹמָם}}.</ref>—Moreover, cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֹֽרַנִּית|translate=backward}}, and {{GHGheb|text=קְדֹֽרַנִּית|translate=darkly attired}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=3|verse=14}}. In both these cases, the formative syllable ''an'' has been first attached to the stem, and then the feminine ending ''îth'', which is elsewhere used to form adverbs, has been added to it.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|h}}
The termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}} occurs also in the formation of substantives, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אוּלָם|translate=porch}}, and hence the above adverbs may equally well be regarded as nouns used adverbially, so that {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֹם}}, would correspond to {{GHGheb|text=־ָן}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹן}} (§ 85, Nos. 53, 54), cf. {{GHGheb|text=בְּפִתְאֹם}} (with prep.) ''suddenly'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=36}}. According to others, this ''am'' is an obsolete accusative ending, to be compared with the indeterminate accusative sing. in ''ăn'' in Arabic.<section end=par100 /><noinclude>
